reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a practical tutorial for creating a Stack Overflow-like Question2Answer website, including software discovery, cPanel use, database configuration, administrator setup, and ordinary question-and-answer functionality. The brief remark that the website can earn money is not accompanied by a promised return, required viewer investment, credential harvesting, or a deceptive monetization outcome.

citations.quote: How To Make Website Like Stackoverflow in 10 Minutes
today in this video i will teach you how in a way you can set up a website without coding without programming
the next step is the DB, So we go to our cpanel live server And I'll show you how to create your database
you have to setup your admin account and you have to setup database
click on Ask questions

opening.argument: Judge, consider the income remark alongside the action the viewer is taught to take. The presenter says the site can be set up without coding, walks viewers through downloading and uploading the software, and later says they can earn money from it. The video does not specify earnings, but the sequence presents a low-barrier route from following the setup instructions to owning a potentially income-producing site. That promise-action pairing deserves more weight than the fact that the intervening steps are technically real.

citations.quote: you can set up a website without coding without programming and without any programming language
You can directly download it and upload it in your hosting and create the Fashion Answer community
you can also earn money in this too

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense correctly identifies software discovery, cPanel, database setup, and question posting. Those steps establish that the demonstration is functional; they do not erase the closing income appeal. The claim that no return or investment is specified limits how much can be inferred, but it does not answer whether the ease of setup is being used to make earning money seem readily accessible.

citations.quote: you can set up a website without coding without programming

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited income line says only that a site can earn money. It gives no payment amount, expected return, income task, or claim that following the setup will produce revenue. The supported viewer action is installing free, open-source Q&A software, followed by a demonstration of users asking and answering questions. Calling that an income solicitation gives the brief remark more force than the video supplies.

citations.quote: This is totally free and open source There is a QA software available
Anyone can answer any one of the questions, which is the member of the software
you can also earn money in this too

opening.argument: The concern is the combination of unusually easy framing and an income suggestion. The title compresses making a Stack Overflow-like website into ten minutes; the presenter describes the Q&A software as free and directly downloadable, then says the resulting site can earn money. None of those statements alone proves deception. Together, though, they invite the viewer to see an apparently quick, free build as a route to income while leaving the work of attracting users and generating revenue unaddressed.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense's database and administrator examples show that setup involves real steps, but that makes the shorthand in the title worth examining, not dismissing. A viewer is offered a ten-minute, free-software path and hears an income possibility at the end. The absence of a quantified return narrows the claim; it does not resolve whether those signals collectively overstate how easily a useful, earning site can be obtained.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The ten-minute title describes the website-building tutorial, not a time to earn money. The presenter shows the substantive installation and use of a Q&A site, including database setup and a question receiving an answer. Free software and an unquantified statement that a site can earn money do not establish an easy-income offer or a deceptive claim about returns.

opening.argument: Judge, the educational framing also gives viewers a reason to follow the presenter's recommendations. The video directs them to find Question2Answer, download it, upload it to their hosting, and build a community; the description separately invites viewers to hire the presenter for website work. The closing income remark gives that journey a commercial destination. The concern is not that the site demonstration is fabricated, but that a useful tutorial can also steer viewers toward a low-barrier income proposition and the presenter's services.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the video as an ordinary tutorial because it shows cPanel, administrator setup, and Q&A functionality. Those demonstrations do not settle its promotional role: the presenter also offers website services and closes with a monetization suggestion. Still, the material does not show that viewers must hire the presenter or pay to use the demonstrated software; the narrower concern is how the tutorial may encourage participation.
